about: The plan for the lines of docs/woodex-os/14-PRODUCTION-TODO.md that are not done: a short title for each, the rounds in which the lines that can start now are done, and for each of those lines what is built and how it is tested. Read with the list by scripts/verify-plan.mjs, which writes docs/woodex-os/21-PENDING-WORK-PLAN-AND-TESTS.md and fails when the three disagree. When a line is done, take it out of its round and out of the titles.

rounds.name: The shop reads its products from `/api/v1`, behind a switch that stays off
rounds.why: P1, and the owner's word of 19 November ("start as you recommend", DL-037). Website Studio and Marketing, 17 of the 36 destinations of Feature status that are not open, wait for this line and then for the page builder (T-115); the Orders screen waits for it too. It is the first address of `/api/v1` in pages and the first that hands out money, so the rules of T-063 are tried on it before anything else is built on them.

lines.found: Read in the code on 19 November; nothing of it is built. The shop reads its products from its own Node API (`/api/products`, and `/api/products/overrides` for changed prices and stock), which reads the shop's database: the 148 sample products (D-007). Categories, series and pictures it can already read from `/api/v1`, through two bridges of the Node API, behind a switch that is off. `/api/v1` has no address for products. Laravel keeps each of the 170 real products as a draft and a published copy; all 170 are drafts, and publishing one asks for a review, a category, a price, a description, the shipping and warranty texts, a picture with its description, and a preview seen by the person who publishes (D-009, T-090). The basket prices its lines from the sales catalogue by the shop's own product number, not from these products.
build: `GET /api/v1/catalogue/products`, in pages, and one product by its address: only the published copy of a product that is not archived, never the draft. Prices as whole paisa with the currency, times in UTC, the filters the contract names (category, series, changed since) and no other. Written into `platform/resources/api/v1.openapi.json` and document 29 first.
The pictures of a published product at an address of their own, as the categories' pictures are.

A bridge in the shop's Node API and a reader in the React shop that turn the answer into the product the pages use today, behind a switch of the shop that stays off. With the switch off the shop reads exactly what it reads today.
How a basket of products read from Laravel is priced: the round decides it, records the decision, and a test sends such a basket.
tests: The contract test names the new routes, and each answer is compared with the contract key by key: success, a page beyond the last, a filter that is not allowed (400), a product that is not published (404), too many requests (429).
A draft, a withdrawn product and an archived one are never handed out, by the list or by their own address; what is handed out is the published copy, also when the draft was changed after it.
Money arrives as whole paisa; a product without a price is "on request" and carries no figure; a sale price is handed out only between its two dates.

The shop's reader is run against the answers the contract documents, in CI's `build-and-test`, and against a real answer of Laravel on the rehearsal: the same name, price and pictures arrive in the product the pages use.
With the switch off the shop asks Laravel nothing: its build and its existing scripts give what they gave before.
After the merge the outside check asks the products address on the live demo.
browser: On the rehearsal a product is published in the admin by a browser. The shop's bridge, pointed at that rehearsal, hands it to the shop's reader, and the product is shown with its name, price and picture. Withdrawn in the admin, it is gone from the shop.
lines.against: With the draft handed out in place of the published copy, the test of the unpublished product names it; with the shop's reader left reading rupees where paisa arrive, its script names the price.
lines.back: The shop's switch stays off: the live shop reads what it reads today, and the round changes no setting of either Vercel project. The new addresses hand out only published products, and none is published on the demo. The Node catalogue is not closed in this round.

rounds.name: What the merge of pull request #52 left to read from the live site
rounds.why: Three small lines whose building is merged and whose proof can only come from the live site: Vercel's own network cannot be rehearsed, a cold start cannot be ordered, and GitHub starts a timer when it will. Nothing is built here; each line is closed by reading, and the readings are written down at the start of the next round.

lines.found: Built and merged with pull request #52: the eight built files with a marked name are sent with one year and `immutable` by a rule in the part of `vercel.json` that Vercel applies to a file it has found. The root test reads the rule against the build's manifest, and the rehearsal asks for each file through it. The live site was read before the merge, on 20 November at 13:55 UTC, when it still ran the old build: `max-age=0`. Vercel's own network cannot be rehearsed, so that it applies the rule is not proved until it is read from outside.
build: Nothing more is built. The outside check from `main` requires one year on the stylesheet that the sign-in page names, and 404 without a long life for a built file with a marked name that does not exist.
tests: The outside check's run after the merge of pull request #52, and the next timed run, are read: both must say one year for the stylesheet.

If Vercel's network does not apply the rule, the check fails by itself and opens an issue. The first thing to try then is the flag `important: true` on the same rule: Vercel's own builder for Next.js sets it on its one-year rule in the same place (`@vercel/next` 31.0.1), and the routing schema calls it deprecated. The second is the rule as a route before the file is looked up, the older documented way, which may also reach a marked name that is no file. Vercel's `headers` setting is no way out while `vercel.json` uses `routes`: the two were not allowed together in the last version of Vercel's tool whose code can be read. Whatever is tried is rehearsed first.
lines.against: Done before the merge: with the rule taken out, the root test and the rehearsal fail; with the rule widened to every built file, both fail on `site.css`. On the branch the outside check read `max-age=0` and only noted it, because the live site was the old one.
lines.back: A file with a marked name never changes under that name, so a long life cannot serve an old file. One entry of `vercel.json` to take out.

lines.found: Built and merged with pull request #52: an answer for which the function had to be started carries the header `X-Woodex-Cold-Start: 1`, and the outside check times its first request and says whether it carried the mark. Read once before the merge, on the old build, which says nothing: 2.29 s to the first byte on 20 November at 13:55 UTC from a GitHub runner; warm it is 0.08 to 0.17 s. No cold reading with the mark exists yet.
build: Nothing more is built. Each run of the outside check prints the time of its first request and whether that answer carried the mark.
tests: Three readings that carried the mark, each with its date and where it was asked from, are written into `13-VERCEL-DEPLOYMENT.md` §9. A reading without the mark is a warm one and is not counted.
lines.against: Done before the merge: with the mark taken out of the entry file the rehearsal fails once; with the mark sent on every answer it fails twice.
lines.back: One header on an answer, and a line of output.
lines.unknown: How often the check meets a copy that has just started. After a merge it very likely does; a timed run may find the function warm. If three cold readings do not come by themselves within a week, the line says so and stays open.

lines.found: Read on 20 November at 14:24 UTC: six timed runs since the timer came to `main` on 17 November, for thirteen times due. The times due at 06:23 and 18:23 UTC brought a run every time, 1 h 08 min to 2 h 43 min late; the times due at 00:23 and 12:23 UTC never. Four runs are green; the two of 18 and 19 November failed on a point of the check itself (a preview that Vercel had removed answered 410, where the check accepted only the sign-in: issue #46, cured with pull request #47). Of the last four times due, two brought a run, so the timer was written again with pull request #52: 03:47, 09:47, 15:47 and 21:47 UTC. Starting the check by hand is refused to this session (HTTP 403). The check after a merge has run every time.
build: Nothing more is built. GitHub's list of timed runs is read at the start of every round, and how many of the times due brought a run is written into the list.

If the new minute does no better after eight times due, the line says that GitHub does not keep a six-hourly timer for this repository, and the owner is asked whether twice a day is enough or another service should start the check.
tests: Runs started by the timer are in GitHub's list for at least three of the last four times due at the new minute, and they are green.
lines.against: Done on 17 November: a forced failure opened issue #38, and the next proof closed it.

rounds.name: The dashboard
rounds.why: P1. The first screen every person sees. In the order you set for the design work it comes before the areas (DL-008).

lines.found: The dashboard is one component with one view: figures for a period, six live queues, what needs attention, the pipeline, new leads, recent activity.
build: Each block becomes a widget under one contract: who may see it and with which module, its figure, its link, and its states: loading, empty, error, no access.

The missing widgets: the sales funnel with its conversion rate; overdue amounts by age and payables due; the health and milestones of projects. Every chart states its dates, its currency and its definition.
A widget whose module is switched off is absent, not empty.
tests: For every widget with a figure: its link opens a list of exactly that many rows. The records are made in the test, some of them at the edges of the period in Pakistan time.
Every widget in every state. A widget that fails shows its own error, and the rest of the dashboard is still drawn.
As each role: only the widgets that role may see. With a module off, its widget is not in the page.
The number of database queries the dashboard makes is written down as a limit.
browser: The crawl as four roles at both widths.
A journey step follows two figures to their lists and compares the numbers on the screen.
lines.against: With one widget's count changed to include one more state, the first test fails.
lines.back: Views and queries that only read. No record changes.

What the journey finds is corrected in the same round.
tests: The journey runs with the other two, in the sandbox and in CI.
A test reads every dialog for its name, and every field with an error for the link to its message.
lines.against: With the dialog no longer keeping the focus inside, the journey fails at that step.
lines.back: Tests, and small corrections to views.
lines.yours: After it, one person of your team does the same without a mouse, and with a screen reader if one is at hand. Gate A asks for that review.

lines.found: The top bar has the search, "Create new", the colour theme, the notifications and the account. It has no help entry, and no pinned or recent screens. A person's record has no place for such preferences yet.
build: A Help entry in the top bar: what this screen is for, the keyboard shortcuts, and the request number to give when asking for help.
A screen can be pinned from its heading; pinned screens stand at the head of the menu. The screens opened last are listed, for each person.
Both are kept with the person, in one small table added by a migration.
tests: Pinned and recent screens are remembered for each person and are still there after signing out and in.
Nobody is shown another person's; a screen the person may no longer open is not offered.
All of it by keyboard, in the journey of T-054.
browser: The crawl at both widths; the keyboard journey pins a screen and opens it from the menu.
lines.against: With the check of the person's rights taken out, "is not offered" fails.
lines.back: One migration that only adds; its way back removes the table.

rounds.name: Every shared part on one screen; a slow list and a lost connection

lines.found: No screen shows the shared parts side by side. The parts are 25 files in `platform/resources/views/components/admin` and the three parts of the table beside them; their rules are written there since 20 November (`README.md`). A new screen is a 69th destination: the registry of destinations, Feature status and the tests that count destinations change with it.

Buttons, badges, cards, fields with and without an error, the empty state, the dialog, the toast, the page links, and the table in its five states.
The destination is added to the registry with its permission, so that the menu, Feature status and the route agree.
tests: The screen opens for owner and admin and is refused to the other roles.
A test lists the files under `components/admin`: a part that is not drawn on the screen, and is not on a short written list of parts that cannot stand alone, fails it.
The table's five states on the screen are read with the words and roles the component's own test reads.
browser: The crawl opens it at 1366 px and 390 px: no console error, nothing wider than the window. It is looked at in the dark theme, and one picture of it goes into the report for gate A.
lines.against: With one part taken off the screen, the test that lists the parts names it.
lines.back: A screen that changes no record. It can be taken out of the registry alone.

lines.found: No screen says "loading": a Livewire screen arrives with its rows, and no component is loaded late. `wire:loading` is written 117 times in 64 views, to dim rows or to stop a button being pressed twice. Nothing tells a person that the connection is lost: `wire:offline` is written nowhere and no script listens for it, so a press then does nothing and says nothing. The shared table has had a loading state since 20 November (T-041).
build: A notice in the top bar while the browser is offline or the server does not answer, and that it is back when it is: said to a screen reader, and never laid over the form a person is typing in.
A press that could not be sent says so, and what was typed stays.

With the network slowed on the rehearsal, each list of the shared table is timed. A list that is slow there is loaded late and draws the table's loading state first; a list that arrives in time is left as it is, and the report names both kinds.
tests: A test draws the notice and reads its words and its role.
For each list that is loaded late: what stands there first is the table's loading state, and the rows that follow are the rows of before.
browser: A journey step cuts the network with the browser's own switch, presses Save on a form, reads the notice, brings the network back and saves: nothing typed is lost.
With the network slowed, the placeholder of a late list is seen and then replaced by its rows.
lines.against: With the notice taken out, the journey step fails where it reads it.
lines.back: Views and one small script; the built files change. The notice can be taken out alone, and a late list made an early one again by one word.

rounds.name: Lighter pages; nothing smaller than 12 px
rounds.why: Both change the same shared parts: the menu, the top bar, the search.

Then, as far as the measurement says: each icon drawn once and referred to; the search's list of screens fetched when the search is first opened; the phone's menu made of the same markup as the sidebar.
tests: A test holds a near-empty page under 60 KB of HTML and prints the size of each part.
The crawl prints the median size of all pages.
The journeys that use the search, the menu and the phone's drawer pass.
browser: Both journeys and the crawl at both widths.
lines.against: The size test fails on today's page.

lines.found: 19 places in 14 views, and 7 rules of the stylesheets, set text below 12 px: from 8 px (the line under the logo) to 11 px.

rounds.name: The content policy without `eval`
rounds.why: After the rounds that replace whole parts of the views (the table, the dashboard, the top bar, the menu), so that nothing is converted twice; and before the screen pass, which its test then holds to the strict form from the first view.

lines.found: About 200 Alpine expressions in the views: 21 `x-data`, 19 of them written out in the markup; 121 handlers of events; 30 `x-show`.

`'unsafe-eval'` leaves the policy.

browser: Both journeys, and every screen as four roles at both widths. The scripts already fail on anything the browser refuses.
lines.against: With one arrow function left in a view, the crawl reports the refusal and fails.

lines.back: Views and the stylesheet only; one area in one pull request.
